newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees lower Q2 North American output.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees lower Q2 North American output.

text.p: Ford Motor Co on Friday said it planned to build 472,000 cars and 730,000 trucks in North America in the second quarter, or a total of 1,202,000 vehicles.
That represents a decline of less than one percent from the 1,213,000 vehicles made in the second quarter of 1996. In the year-earlier period, Ford produced 538,000 cars and 675,000 trucks.

On a regional basis, Ford plans to build 356,000 cars and 606,000 trucks in the United States in the second quarter of this year; 65,000 cars and 103,000 trucks in Canada; and 51,000 cars and 21,000 trucks in Mexico.

Ford revised its first-quarter North American production schedule to show a slight increase on earlier estimates. The automaker plans to build 19,000 fewer cars and 21,000 additional trucks in the first quarter. Total first quarter production is now estimated at 1,037,000 vehicles.

Ford is the second of Detrot's Big Three to release a second-quarter production forecast. On Thursday, General Motors Corp said it planned to build 1,550,000 cars and trucks, about the same as during the year-ago period.
